topics.title: Friction
topics.subject: physics
outcomes: understand the concept of friction in everyday life contexts (u)

body.text: Friction is a force that opposes relative motion (or attempted motion) between two surfaces in contact. It acts along the surfaces, in the direction opposite to the motion.

Friction is not always unwanted. It lets us walk without slipping, lets tyres grip the road, and lets brakes stop a moving vehicle. But it also wastes energy as heat and wears surfaces down over time, for example in engine parts, shoe soles, and tyre tread.
Friction can be reduced by smoothing or polishing surfaces, or by adding a lubricant such as oil or grease. It can be increased by roughening a surface, for example the tread pattern cut into a tyre.
Use the PhET Friction simulation below. Rub the two surfaces together and watch how friction between them generates heat.
